notes: Product scanner rules. Labels are decided by rules, never by a score (see src/engine/scanner.ts); the ingredient grade below is shown beside the label and never changes it. Worth limiting: an IARC Group 1 or 2A item, or NOVA 4 with added sugar or salt above the WHO (PAHO) thresholds. Fine in moderation: NOVA 3 or 4 with no Group 1 or 2A item, or any Group 2B additive, or a WCRF risk item. No cancer evidence: nothing on the IARC or WCRF risk lists. Protective WCRF items are shown separately and do not change the label. A rule with "lead": true only counts its words among the first three ingredients, so 8% milk powder in a sweet spread is not 'dairy' and wine cooked into a sauce is not 'alcohol' (category tags and the alcohol figure still count). 'exclude' phrases are removed before matching (goat cheese is not red meat). Products tagged with a 'meatFreeTags' category are never matched as meat. Every quote is in the source's own words; 'quoteChecked' turns true once the clinical reviewer confirms it against the live page.

source.name: WHO Regional Office for the Americas (PAHO) Nutrient Profile Model, 2016

grade.notes: The ingredient grade, A to F, shown for every product and item looked up (added at the product owner's request, October 2026). Each item linked to cancer in a product adds points once, by how strong the evidence is that it can cause cancer: IARC Group 1, Group 2A, a WCRF 'probable' cause, Group 2B, and ultra-processing with added sugar or salt over the WHO (PAHO) limits (linked to weight gain). 'limited' is for diary foods with only limited evidence. Protective foods add nothing and take nothing away. The grade counts items, not amounts: it cannot tell a trace from a main ingredient, or how much a person eats. Bands are the lowest point total for each grade. Changing points or bands changes the grade of every product in content/products: run npm run grades afterwards (a test checks).
